[Lecture Map]{.slide-title}

<hr>

::: {.body-text-m}
- **Unit:** Unit V - Emerging Technologies
- **Course Outcome:** CO5 - Illustrate the emerging trends and technologies in the field of Information Technology
- **Bloom's Levels:** K1 - Remember; K2 - Understand
- **Duration:** 50 minutes, including a 3-minute activity and 5-minute knowledge check; reference slides are for self-study
- **Central Question:** How do organisations turn enormous, fast-growing, and messy data into useful decisions?

---

## {data-menu-title="Learning Objectives"}

[Learning Objectives]{.slide-title}

<hr>

::: {.body-text-m}
By the end of this lecture, students will be able to:

- define big data and big data analytics;
- explain the 5 Vs of big data;
- distinguish structured, semi-structured, and unstructured data;
- describe the big data analytics process and the types of analytics;
- name common big data technologies and explain how they work;
- state the limitations and challenges of big data analytics;
- identify major application areas of big data analytics.
:::

---

## {data-menu-title="Think About It"}

[Think About It]{.slide-title}

<hr>

::: {.body-text-m}
- Every minute, millions of searches, messages, videos, and payments are generated. Where does all that data go?
- How does an online shop know what you may want to buy **next**?
- Can a spreadsheet handle **a billion rows**?
- Could data help predict **traffic jams, diseases, or loan defaults** before they happen?
:::

---

## {data-menu-title="Why Big Data?"}

[Why Has Data Become "Big"?]{.slide-title2}

<hr>

::: {.body-text-m}
- **Internet and social media:** billions of users create posts, photos, and videos.
- **Smartphones and IoT:** sensors continuously generate readings.
- **Digital payments and e-commerce:** every transaction is recorded.
- **Cheaper storage and computing:** keeping and processing data is now affordable.
- **Digital government and healthcare:** records, scans, and services move online.
- A single database server **may become impractical** when volume, speed, variety, or cost exceeds its capabilities; distributed systems are one response.
:::

---

## {data-menu-title="What Is Big Data?"}

[What Is Big Data?]{.slide-title2}

<hr>

::: {.body-text-m}
**Big data** refers to datasets that are so **large, fast-growing, and varied** that traditional tools cannot easily store, process, or analyse them.

**Big data analytics** is the process of examining such data to discover **patterns, trends, correlations, and useful insights** that support better decisions.

- Sources: social media, sensors and IoT devices, online transactions, mobile apps, logs, medical records, and satellite images.
:::

---

## {data-menu-title="Data Units"}

[How Big Is Big?]{.slide-title2}

<hr>

::: {.body-text-s}
| Unit | Approximate Size | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Gigabyte (GB) | 1,000 MB | A movie file |
| Terabyte (TB) | 1,000 GB | A large personal hard disk |
| Petabyte (PB) | 1,000 TB | Data of a large company in a day |
| Exabyte (EB) | 1,000 PB | Internet traffic of a region |
| Zettabyte (ZB) | 1,000 EB | Global data created in a year |
:::

---

## {data-menu-title="The 5 Vs"}

[The 5 Vs of Big Data]{.slide-title2}

<hr>

::: {.body-text-s}
| V | Meaning | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Volume | Very large amount of data | Petabytes of video and transaction data |
| Velocity | Speed at which data is generated and processed | Live stock prices, sensor streams |
| Variety | Many formats and sources | Text, images, audio, logs, sensor data |
| Veracity | Accuracy and trustworthiness of data | Fake reviews, missing or noisy values |
| Value | Useful insight gained from the data | Better decisions, new services, higher profit |
:::

---

## {data-menu-title="Types of Data"}

[Structured, Semi-Structured, and Unstructured Data]{.slide-title2}

<hr>

::: {.body-text-s}
| Type | Description | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| Structured | Fixed format in rows and columns | Bank records, student marks tables |
| Semi-structured | Has tags or keys but flexible layout | JSON, XML, email headers, log files |
| Unstructured | No predefined tabular schema | Text, images, audio, video, social media posts |
:::

::: {.body-text-m}
Big data can include **all three types**; their proportions depend on the application. Text and media can be stored as database values or files, but analysing their content needs suitable tools.
:::

---

## {data-menu-title="Features of Big Data Analytics"}

[Key Features of Big Data Analytics]{.slide-title2}

<hr>

::: {.body-text-m}
- **Handles huge data:** works on data too large for a single machine.
- **Distributed processing:** data and computation are spread across many machines in parallel.
- **Real-time and batch analysis:** can analyse streams with low latency or process stored data later.
- **Works with all data types:** structured, semi-structured, and unstructured.
- **Scalable and flexible:** capacity grows by adding more nodes, often in the cloud.
- **Supports prediction:** uncovers hidden patterns and forecasts future trends.
:::

---

## {data-menu-title="Analytics Process"}

[The Big Data Analytics Process]{.slide-title2}

<hr>

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    A[1. Collect Data] --> B[2. Store Data]
    B --> C[3. Clean and Prepare]
    C --> D[4. Process and Analyse]
    D --> E[5. Visualise and Interpret]
    E --> F[6. Decide and Act]
```

::: {.body-text-s}
- **Collect and store:** gather data from many sources into distributed storage.
- **Clean and prepare:** correct errors, handle duplicates, and treat missing values appropriately.
- **Process and analyse:** apply statistics, data mining, and machine learning.
- **Visualise and act:** show results as dashboards and charts to support decisions.
:::

---

## {data-menu-title="Types of Analytics"}

[Types of Big Data Analytics]{.slide-title2}

<hr>

::: {.body-text-s}
| Type | Question Answered | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Descriptive | What happened? | Monthly sales report |
| Diagnostic | Why did it happen? | Finding why sales fell in one region |
| Predictive | What is likely to happen? | Forecasting customer churn |
| Prescriptive | What should we do? | Recommending the best delivery route |
:::

---

## {data-menu-title="Batch vs Stream"}

[Batch Processing vs Stream Processing]{.slide-title2}

<hr>

::: {.body-text-s}
| Feature | Batch Processing | Stream (Real-Time) Processing |
|---|---|---|
| Data | Large stored datasets | Continuous flow of data |
| Timing | Results after the job finishes | Results within seconds or milliseconds |
| Example | Monthly billing, yearly sales analysis | Fraud alerts, live traffic updates |
| Typical tools | Hadoop MapReduce | Spark Structured Streaming, Kafka Streams |
:::

---

## {data-menu-title="Hadoop and MapReduce"}

[How Big Data Is Processed: Hadoop and MapReduce]{.slide-title2}

<hr>

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    D[Huge Dataset] --> S[Split into blocks across many nodes]
    S --> M1[Map task 1]
    S --> M2[Map task 2]
    S --> M3[Map task 3]
    M1 --> R[Shuffle and Reduce]
    M2 --> R
    M3 --> R
    R --> O[Final Result]
```

::: {.body-text-s}
- **HDFS** stores data in blocks, replicated across nodes for fault tolerance.
- **Map** transforms input records into key-value pairs; **shuffle** groups values by key; **Reduce** aggregates each group. Tasks run across nodes.
- The idea is the same as in grid computing: **divide, distribute, combine**.
:::

---

## {data-menu-title="Big Data Tools"}

[Technologies Used for Big Data]{.slide-title2}

<hr>

::: {.body-text-m}
- **Hadoop and HDFS:** distributed storage and batch processing across clusters.
- **MapReduce:** splits a job into map and reduce steps that run in parallel.
- **Apache Spark:** distributed processing for batch and streams; can cache data in memory and also use disk.
- **Apache Kafka:** publishes, stores, and delivers event streams; **Kafka Streams** provides stream-processing operations.
- **NoSQL databases:** document, wide-column, and other non-relational stores; schema flexibility and scaling depend on the system.
- **Data warehouses and data lakes:** central stores for analysis.
- **Visualisation tools:** Power BI, Tableau, and similar dashboards.
:::

---

## {data-menu-title="Warehouse vs Lake"}

[Data Warehouse vs Data Lake]{.slide-title2}

<hr>

::: {.body-text-s}
| Feature | Data Warehouse | Data Lake |
|---|---|---|
| Data stored | Usually curated data for analysis | Raw or processed data in many formats |
| Schema | Usually defined before loading | Often applied when reading |
| Users | Business analysts | Data scientists and engineers |
| Purpose | Reports and dashboards | Exploration, machine learning, big analysis |
:::

---

## {data-menu-title="Big Data and Cloud"}

[Big Data, Cloud, and Machine Learning]{.slide-title2}

<hr>

::: {.body-text-m}
- **Cloud computing** supplies storage and processing on demand, so organisations need not own huge clusters. (Recall Unit IV: AWS, Google, Microsoft, IBM.)
- **IoT** (Unit III) produces much of the streaming data.
- **Machine learning and AI** find patterns in big data to predict and recommend.
- **Grid and cluster computing** (Lecture 27) supply the parallel processing power behind large analysis jobs.
:::

---

## {data-menu-title="Advantages"}

[Advantages of Big Data Analytics]{.slide-title2}

<hr>

::: {.body-text-m}
- **Better decisions** based on evidence rather than guesswork.
- **Personalisation:** tailored products, offers, and recommendations.
- **Early detection:** fraud, faults, and disease outbreaks spotted sooner.
- **Operational efficiency:** optimised supply chains, energy use, and routes.
- **New products and revenue** created from data insights.
:::

---

## {data-menu-title="Big Data Limitations"}

[Limitations and Challenges of Big Data Analytics]{.slide-title2}

<hr>

::: {.body-text-m}
- **Privacy and security:** large collections of personal data can be misused or leaked.
- **Data quality:** noisy, biased, or incomplete data leads to wrong conclusions.
- **Storage and processing cost:** infrastructure and skilled staff are expensive.
- **Shortage of skills:** data scientists and engineers are in high demand.
- **Integration problems:** combining data from different formats and systems is hard.
- **Ethical issues:** algorithmic bias and unfair decisions.
- **Governance and compliance:** follow applicable data-protection requirements, obtain appropriate permissions, and limit collection and retention.
:::

---

## {data-menu-title="Big Data Applications"}

[Application Areas of Big Data Analytics]{.slide-title2}

<hr>

::: {.body-text-s}
| Area | Use of Big Data Analytics |
|---|---|
| Business and retail | Customer behaviour, recommendations, demand forecasting |
| Banking and finance | Fraud detection, credit scoring, risk analysis |
| Healthcare | Disease prediction, patient monitoring, drug research |
| Transport and logistics | Route optimisation, traffic prediction |
| Social media and marketing | Sentiment analysis, targeted advertising |
| Government and smart cities | Policy planning, crime prevention, utility management |
| Agriculture | Crop yield prediction and weather-based advice |
| Telecom | Churn prediction and network optimisation |
:::

---

## {data-menu-title="Case Study"}

[Illustrative Case: Recommendations on an Online Store]{.slide-title2}

<hr>

::: {.body-text-m}
- **Data collected:** clicks, searches, purchases, ratings, and time spent on each page from millions of users.
- **Processing:** the data is stored in a distributed system and analysed with Spark and machine-learning models.
- **Insight:** customers who buy a phone often buy a cover and a charger soon after.
- **Action:** the site shows personalised suggestions and sends timely offers.
- **Concern:** how much personal data should be tracked, and how should it be protected?

**Lesson:** value comes not from the data itself but from the **insight and action** derived from it.
:::

## {data-menu-title="Summary"}

[Lecture Summary]{.slide-title}

<hr>

::: {.body-text-m}
- Big data is characterised by the 5 Vs: Volume, Velocity, Variety, Veracity, and Value.
- Data may be structured, semi-structured, or unstructured; the mix depends on the use case.
- The process runs from collection and storage to cleaning, analysis, visualisation, and decision.
- Analytics may be descriptive, diagnostic, predictive, or prescriptive.
- Hadoop, MapReduce, Spark, Kafka, and NoSQL databases are common technologies.
- Challenges include privacy, data quality, cost, skills, and ethics.
:::

## {data-menu-title="Knowledge Check"}

[Knowledge Check: MCQs]{.slide-title2}

<hr>

::: {.body-text-s}
1. Which of these is NOT one of the 5 Vs of big data?  
   A. Volume  B. Velocity  C. Veracity  D. Vulnerability  
   **Answer: D**

2. Photos, audio, and videos are examples of:  
   A. Structured data  B. Unstructured data  C. Only metadata  D. Source code  
   **Answer: B**

3. Predictive analytics mainly answers:  
   A. What happened?  B. Why did it happen?  C. What is likely to happen?  D. Who is responsible?  
   **Answer: C**

4. HDFS is used in Hadoop for:  
   A. Distributed file storage  B. Drawing graphics  C. Editing documents  D. Playing music  
   **Answer: A**

5. A major challenge of big data analytics is:  
   A. Privacy and data quality  B. Data never grows  C. It needs no computers  D. It has no applications  
   **Answer: A**
:::

## {data-menu-title="Key Concepts"}

[Important Definitions and Key Terminology]{.slide-title2}

<hr>

::: {.body-text-s}
- **Big data:** very large, fast, and varied data that needs special tools to process.
- **5 Vs:** Volume, Velocity, Variety, Veracity, and Value.
- **Structured / semi-structured / unstructured:** data with fixed, partial, or no predefined format.
- **Hadoop and HDFS:** framework and file system for distributed storage and processing.
- **MapReduce:** programming model that splits work into map and reduce steps.
- **Apache Spark:** distributed analytics engine with in-memory caching capabilities.
- **NoSQL:** non-relational databases for flexible, large-scale data.
- **Data warehouse / data lake:** stores for structured or raw data.
- **Data mining:** discovering patterns in large datasets.
:::
